LESSON: GUIDED READING : READING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.9: Guided reading : Reading comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided reading : Reading comprehension, part of Reading in Grade 8 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: Why should we read texts with correct speed?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. read a text with correct speed and expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided reading : Reading comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. apply appropriate intonation and stress when reading texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided reading : Reading comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. develop interest in reading Arabic texts for enjoyment.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided reading : Reading comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. read a text with correct speed and expression,

   Guided reading : Reading comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. apply appropriate intonation and stress when reading texts,

   Guided reading : Reading comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. develop interest in reading Arabic texts for enjoyment.

   Guided reading : Reading comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read short sentences on greetings and self-introduction aloud with correct pronunciation,

2. collaborate with peers to review each other’s reading speed for fluency and accuracy,

3. identify words in the Arabic language that bring different meaning

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read short sentences on greetings and self-introduction aloud with correct pronunciation,
2. collaborate with peers to review each other’s reading speed for fluency and accuracy,
3. identify words in the Arabic language that bring different meaning

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided reading : Reading comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: This is enhanced as the learner is motivated to learn continually by peer reviewing each other’s reading

speed for fluency and accuracy.

• Critical thinking and Problem solving: This is promoted as the learner follows simple instructions to identify words in the

Arabic language that bring different meaning when stress and intonation is applied differently.

21

Values:
Unity: This is promoted as the learner cooperates with peers to compose a narrative on the theme.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: This is promoted as the learner works with peers to familiarise with greetings across the society for peaceful

living.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept on greetings and introductions for social cohesion to their learning of similar concepts in

English.
